title: Table 1.01 The WHO Reporting System for Breast Cytopathology: risk of malignancy and recommendations for further diagnostic management
tablehtml:
Diagnostic category

Estimated ROMa

Clinical management optionsb

Insufficient / Inadequate / Non-diagnostic

0–60.9%

CORRELATE. Repeat FNAB or consider CNB. If low clinical suspicion, consider repeat clinical and imaging examination in 3–6 months.

Benign

0–11.7%

CORRELATE. If discrepancy, repeat FNAB and/or perform CNB. If correlation, follow up at appropriate interval.

Atypical

13.0–40.0%

CORRELATE. Repeat FNAB and/or perform CNB. If low clinical suspicion, consider repeat clinical and imaging examination in 3–6 months.

Suspicious

45.8–100%

CORRELATE. CNB or excision surgical biopsy; when CNB is not available, consider repeat FNAB or excision surgical biopsy.

Malignant

91.1–100%

CORRELATE. If clinical or imaging discordant, CNB; if clinical and imaging concordant, treat per clinical stage.

CORRELATE, correlate with clinical and imaging findings in the triple test

aEstimated ROMs are based on retrospective and prospective studies on the International Academy of Cytology Yokohama System for Reporting Breast Fine Needle Aspiration Biopsy Cytopathology {30783035; 31524134; 33017520; 30929288; 32749785; 31108486; 33755356; 34133084; 34029453; 33629823; 34321772; 34866246; 34876918; 34515039; 34535580; 34703093; 36516743; 36988122}. bWhile options for further management to achieve a specific diagnosis are outlined above, individualized treatment approaches depend on a variety of factors, including clinical and imaging characteristics, overall functional status of the patient, and equipment availability of the treating facility.
